american-golden-pippin.heading: American Golden Pippin
american-golden-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellowish, tender, juicy, nearly melting, with a rich, refreshing, almost vinous, aromatic flavor
american-golden-pippin.note: Warder had mislaid his notes and quotes Downing's description. Synonyms given: Golden Pippin of Downing, New York Greening.

american-summer-pearmain.heading: American Summer Pearmain
american-summer-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellow, exceedingly tender, almost melting, crisp, fine-grained, juicy; Flavor very mild sub-acid, aromatic, deliciously refreshing
american-summer-pearmain.note: 'This delicious apple'; essentially a fruit for the amateur, not profitable for market. August and September.

bailey.heading: Bailey Sweet
bailey.flavour: Flesh yellow, tender, fine-grained, juicy; Flavor very sweet, rich
bailey.note: From Wyoming County, New York; season October; 'A very valuable variety also for stock.'

benoni.heading: Benoni
benoni.flavour: Flesh yellow, fine-grained, juicy; Flavor rich, sub-acid, spicy
benoni.quality: Quality best; Use, dessert, kitchen and market
benoni.note: 'This handsome and delicious early apple'; native of Dedham, Massachusetts; July and August; 'Delicious and profitable.'

chenango.heading: Frank or Chenango
chenango.flavour: Flesh tender, juicy; Flavor sub-acid, aromatic
chenango.note: Synonym Chenango Strawberry; also called Late Strawberry, so Warder prefers the local name Frank. Native of New York; autumn.

detroit-red.heading: Detroit Black
detroit-red.flavour: Flesh whitish, tender, breaking, juicy; Flavor acid, poor
detroit-red.quality: Quality second to third rate; Use, kitchen and drying
detroit-red.note: Sub-heading 'Detroit Red?--Grand Sachem'. Warder lumps Black and Red Detroit together as very much alike, but adds 'The Red variety may be distinct, as it keeps later.' Downing keeps them apart. September and October.

dutch-mignonne.heading: Dutch Mignonne
dutch-mignonne.flavour: Flesh yellowish white, breaking, coarse-grained, juicy; Flavor acid to sub-acid, rich
dutch-mignonne.quality: Quality good to very good; Use, kitchen, market, drying
dutch-mignonne.note: Synonym Reinette Doree; 'A fine large apple from Holland'. Season given as September, October, whereas Downing's Dutch Mignonne keeps December to March and Downing admits confusion over which apple bears the name, hence probable.

english-russet.heading: Poughkeepsie Russet
english-russet.flavour: Flesh greenish, firm, inclined to be tough; Flavor acid, poor
english-russet.quality: Quality third rate; Use, market and cooking only
english-russet.storage: valued because it keeps soundly for a long time; Season, December until June.
english-russet.note: Synonym English Russet; origin New York. Warder's separate entry 'English Russet' (line 18653) is a different apple, as Downing points out.

fallawater.heading: Fallawater
fallawater.flavour: Flesh whitish, often greenish-white, light, tender, juicy; Flavor very mild sub-acid, or sweet, with little character
fallawater.quality: Quality scarcely good; Use, market and stock
fallawater.storage: Season, November, December, and may be kept longer if desired.
fallawater.note: Synonym Tulpehocken; native of Pennsylvania. 'Essentially a market apple, having little to recommend it but its size, appearance and productiveness.'

golden-harvey.heading: Golden Harvey
golden-harvey.flavour: Flesh yellow, of fine texture, with a rich sub-acid flavor.
golden-harvey.storage: The fruit is apt to shrivel.
golden-harvey.note: Synonym Brandy Apple; rarely seen in American collections, so Warder quotes Downing's description.

golden-sweet.heading: Golden Sweet
golden-sweet.flavour: Flesh yellow, breaking, fine-grained, juicy; Flavor very sweet, aromatic, like sassafrass
golden-sweet.quality: Quality good to very good; Use, baking and market
golden-sweet.note: Synonym Orange Sweeting; from Connecticut; season August - our apple. The 'spice' tag stands for the sassafras-like aroma.

harrison.heading: Harrison
harrison.flavour: Flesh yellow, compact, dry till ripe, then juicy; flavor acid to sub-acid, very rich, saccharine
harrison.quality: Quality good; Use, especially for cider, also for cooking and for dessert in April.
harrison.climate: has been carried westward over a great extent of territory, where it succeeds admirably well
harrison.note: This famous Jersey cider apple, from Essex County, New Jersey.

jefferis.heading: Jefferies
jefferis.flavour: Flesh yellow, breaking, fine-grained, juicy; flavor sub-acid, aromatic, delicious
jefferis.quality: Quality very good, for table and market
jefferis.note: 'This delicious autumn apple originated in Chester County, Pennsylvania'; August to October.

jersey-black.heading: Jersey Black
jersey-black.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, fine-grained, juicy, often stained pink or reddish; Flavor rich, mild sub-acid, aromatic, not spicy, satisfying
jersey-black.quality: Quality good; Use, table, kitchen, cider and for stock
jersey-black.note: Warder says it 'cannot be the Black Apple of Coxe and Downing' (which he describes as Small Black, line 18269), so our aka 'Black Apple' is doubtful.

maiden-blush.heading: Maiden's Blush
maiden-blush.flavour: Flesh white, breaking, fine grained, juicy; Flavor acid, aromatic, and to most palates not agreeable at the dessert, but very good when cooked, and requiring but a short time to be reduced to a delicious pulp of light color.
maiden-blush.note: Native of New Jersey; approved by thirteen of eighteen States reporting to the American Pomological Society; also used for drying. September and October.

melon.heading: Melon
melon.flavour: Flesh yellow, tender, fine grained, juicy; Flavor acid, sub-acid, aromatic, rich
melon.note: Origin East Bloomfield, New York (Norton's Melon) - our apple.

ohio-nonpareil.heading: Ohio Nonpareil
ohio-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh yellowish, tender, fine-grained, juicy; sub-acid, rich
ohio-nonpareil.quality: First quality, for table, market, cooking or drying
ohio-nonpareil.note: Synonyms Myer's Nonpareil, Western Beauty; originated with Mr. Myers near Massillon, Ohio; September to December. Against Hawley, Fall Pippin and others it was declared 'better than the best'.

ortley.heading: Ortley
ortley.flavour: Flesh yellowish, tender, breaking, juicy; Flavor acid to sub-acid, sprightly, refreshing
ortley.note: Synonym White Bellflower 'and many others'; New Jersey. Becoming so defective from scab and bitter-rot that it is disappearing from nurseries; flesh fine enough 'to suit even the invalid'. Acid to sub-acid sits uneasily with our 'mild' tag.

primate.heading: Primate
primate.flavour: Flesh greenish-white, very tender, fine-grained; Flavor mild sub-acid, very agreeable
primate.note: 'This delicious table apple'; skin and flesh too delicate for market. July and August.

pumpkin-sweet.heading: Lyman's Pumpkin Sweet
pumpkin-sweet.flavour: Flesh yellowish, breaking, juicy, often water-cored and heavy; Flavor very sweet
pumpkin-sweet.quality: Quality good; Use, baking and stock-feeding
pumpkin-sweet.note: Synonym Pound Sweet; origin orchard of S. Lyman, Manchester, Connecticut. Warder's separate 'Pumpkin Sweet' (line 14879, Sweet Russet of Ohio, russeted) is a different apple.

reinette-du-canada.heading: Canada Reinette
reinette-du-canada.flavour: Flesh breaking, fine grained, very juicy; Flavor acid to sub-acid, aromatic, rich
reinette-du-canada.quality: Quality very good; Use, table and cooking
reinette-du-canada.storage: Season, December to February, in northern Indiana.
reinette-du-canada.note: Origin uncertain, probably European; Warder omits the synonyms and says the White Pippin is distinct.

sweet-bough.heading: Large Bough
sweet-bough.flavour: Flesh white, very soft, light, juicy; Flavor very sweet when ripe, somewhat bitter when green
sweet-bough.quality: Quality only good--by some called best
sweet-bough.note: Synonym Large Yellow Bough; 'much admired as an early sweet apple'; tasteless when cooked; July and August.

wagener.heading: Wagener
wagener.flavour: Flesh yellowish-white, tender, fine-grained, juicy; Flavor mild sub-acid
wagener.quality: Quality good; Uses, market, table and kitchen
wagener.note: Originated at Penn Yan, Yates County, New York. Downing (1900) instead calls it brisk, somewhat vinous.

white-winter-pearmain.heading: White Winter Pearmain
white-winter-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellow, fine grained, tender, crisp, juicy; Flavor mild sub-acid, very rich
white-winter-pearmain.quality: Quality best; Uses table, kitchen, market
white-winter-pearmain.climate: often scabby on rich limestone soils and on old trees
white-winter-pearmain.note: Brought to Indiana by early pomologists as an unnamed graft; never identified (Downing suggested Winter Harvey); distinct from Michael Henry.

williams-favourite.heading: Williams' Favorite
williams-favourite.flavour: Flesh whitish-yellow, streaked red, breaking, not juicy; Flavor sub-acid, peculiar
williams-favourite.note: Synonym Williams' Early; origin Roxbury, Massachusetts; July and August.
